To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

overexpression of NCED using a circadian and light-responsive promoter results in severe phenotypes in tomato that are not seen with the constitutive promoter and that the rbcS promoter may be more useful for engineering high ABA in crops.

the over-expression of a key enzyme in the biosynthesis of the plant hormone abscisic Acid, in tomato, results in the production of transgenic plants exhibiting a set of symptoms, including photobleaching, reduced chlorophyll content, reduced growth, and interveinal flooding of leaves, that are likely due to the accumulation of very high levels of ABA.

overexpression of LeNCED in tomato under the control of a light-regulated promoter results in severe phenotypic effects that include reduced chlorophyll, carotenoid, and ABA content and reduced growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of transgenic tomato plants with enhanced water-use efficiency.
the design of transgenics with improved water-use efficiency (and other beneficial traits) that do not exhibit negative side effects.
the design of 'high ABA plants' for agriculture, but we also demonstrate that high ABA accumulation is detrimental to plant growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rbcS promoter allows the generation of transgenics with high ABA content but with severe adverse phenotypes.
the rbcS promoter is not a suitable promoter for driving the NCED transgene in tomato.
the rbcS promoter is not suitable to express the LeNCED1 gene in tomato.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of the constitutive GelVin promoter for the over-expression of LeNCEd1 resulted in mild ABA increases, with no negative effects on growth, and the rbcS promoter allowed the generation transgenic lines that accumulated much higher ABA levels and displayed severe negative phenotypes.
the rbcS promoter allows for the generation of transgenics with higher levels of Aba accumulation than with a constitutive promoter, but that these plants exhibit a set of severe symptoms.
over-expression of LeNCEDA in tomato, with the rbcSC promoter, results in very large increases in ABA accumulation, but with negative consequences for plant development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rbcS promoter is an appropriate choice for over-expression of NCEDA in tomato.
the rbcS promoter is a good choice to achieve light- and diurnal regulation of gene expression in plants.
the rbcS promoter allows very high levels of ABA to be produced in a light-responsive manner, but that the negative consequences of such high levels of A BA accumulation may be severe.
